fields.name: I
fields.text: Master interrupt switch: with it at 0 no interrupt runs whatever its own enable says; hardware clears it when an interrupt is taken and RETI sets it again; SEI sets it and CLI clears it.

fields.name: T
fields.text: One-bit holding place for BST (register bit into T) and BLD (T into a register bit).

fields.name: H
fields.text: Set when some arithmetic operations carry out of the low nibble; used in BCD arithmetic.

fields.name: S
fields.text: Sign: always N exclusive-or V.

fields.name: V
fields.text: Set on a two's complement overflow in arithmetic.

fields.name: N
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic result is negative.

fields.name: Z
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic result is zero.

fields.name: C
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic operation produces a carry.

fields.name: EEAR8
fields.text: EEPROM address bit 8, the top bit of EEAR; EEPROM bytes are numbered in order from 0 to the EEPROM size. EEAR starts undefined, so a valid address must be written before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEAR
fields.text: EEPROM address bits 7:0 of EEAR; EEPROM bytes are numbered in order from 0 to the EEPROM size. EEAR starts undefined, so a valid address must be written before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEDR
fields.text: Byte to write into the EEPROM at the EEAR address, or the byte read from the EEPROM at the EEAR address.

fields.name: EEPM
fields.text: Picks what a write of EEPE does: erase and write together, erase only, or write only. Writes here are ignored while EEPE is 1; reset returns them to 0b00 unless an EEPROM programming is under way.

fields.name: EERIE
fields.text: 1 enables the EEPROM Ready interrupt (with SREG.I set), which fires continuously while the non-volatile memory is ready to be programmed; 0 disables it.

fields.name: EEMPE
fields.text: Arms EEPE: with EEMPE at 1, setting EEPE within four clock cycles programs the EEPROM at the chosen address; with it at 0, EEPE does nothing. Hardware clears it four clock cycles after software sets it.

fields.name: EEPE
fields.text: Writing 1 starts EEPROM programming as EEPM selects, provided EEMPE was set to 1 first; hardware clears it when the write time has passed. The CPU stops for two cycles after it is set.

fields.name: EERE
fields.text: Writing 1 reads the EEPROM at the EEAR address; the byte is ready at once and the CPU stops for four cycles. A read, or a change of EEAR, is not possible while a write is under way, so EEPE is checked first.

registers.name: OSCCAL
registers.title: Oscillator Calibration Register
notes: Initial value of bits 7:0 printed as Device Specific Calibration Value.

fields.name: CAL
fields.text: Trims the calibrated internal RC oscillator; the factory value is loaded at reset and software may rewrite it. CAL7 picks the low (0) or high (1) of two overlapping ranges (0x7F runs faster than 0x80); CAL[6:0] tunes within the range from 0x00 (lowest) to 0x7F (highest), each step under 2% in the 7.3 to 8.1 MHz span. EEPROM and Flash write times follow this oscillator: keep it at or below 8.8 MHz while writing them, or the write may fail. Calibration outside the specified range is not guaranteed.

registers.name: CLKPR
registers.title: Clock Prescaler Register
notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.

fields.name: CLKPCE
fields.text: Write 1, with every other CLKPR bit written 0 at the same time, to allow a change of CLKPS; hardware clears it four cycles later or once CLKPS is written. Writing it again inside those four cycles neither extends nor clears it.

fields.name: CLKPS
fields.text: Clock prescaler select: the factor dividing the selected clock source down to the system clock, which slows every synchronous peripheral; may be changed at run time. To change it: write CLKPCE 1 and the rest of CLKPR 0, then within four cycles write the new CLKPS with CLKPCE 0, with interrupts disabled. The CKDIV8 fuse sets the reset value: 0b0000 when unprogrammed, 0b0011 (divide by 8) when programmed, as shipped; the programmed fuse suits a clock source faster than the device's maximum frequency under present conditions. Any value can be written whatever the fuse; software must then pick a large enough factor for such a source.

fields.name: CLKCCE
fields.text: Write 1, with every other CLKCSR bit written 0 at the same time, to allow a change of CLKCSR; hardware clears it four cycles later or once CLKCSR is written. Writing it again inside those four cycles neither extends nor clears it.

fields.name: CLKRDY
fields.text: Clock availability: cleared when a 'Request for Clock Availability' or 'Enable Clock Source' command is entered, set once the selected clock is confirmed running and stable. The time to set varies with start-up time and frequency, and it stays 0 if the clock never runs, so software must tell no clock from not ready yet.

fields.name: CLKC
fields.text: Command given to the clock switch module. To change it: write CLKCCE 1 and the rest of CLKCSR 0, then within 4 cycles write CLKCSR with CLKCCE 0, with interrupts disabled.

values.text: Enable watchdog in automatic reload mode.

registers.name: CLKSELR
registers.title: Clock Selection Register
notes: Initial value of bits 6:0 printed as ~ (CKOUT) SUT[1:0] CKSEL[3:0].

fields.name: COUT
fields.text: Clock output enable used by the 'CKOUT' command; starts as the inverse of the CKOUT fuse and is left alone by 'Recover System Clock Source'.

fields.name: CSUT
fields.text: Start-up time code given with an 'Enable/Disable Clock Source' command; starts as the SUT fuses and is left alone by 'Recover System Clock Source'.

fields.name: CSEL
fields.text: Code of the clock source that goes with the 'Clock Source Switch', 'Request for Clock Availability' and 'Enable/Disable Clock Source' commands; starts as the CKSEL fuses. After 'Recover System Clock Source' it holds the code of the source driving the clock control unit.

fields.name: SM
fields.text: Picks which of the four sleep modes SLEEP enters.

fields.name: SE
fields.text: Must be 1 for SLEEP to put the MCU to sleep; setting it just before SLEEP and clearing it on wake-up is recommended.

fields.name: BODS
fields.text: 1 turns the BOD off during sleep. Set by a timed sequence: write BODS and BODSE both 1, then within four clock cycles write BODS 1 with BODSE 0. It takes hold three clock cycles after being set and hardware clears it after three clock cycles; SLEEP must run while it holds.

fields.name: BODSE
fields.text: Allows BODS to be set, as part of the timed BOD-disable sequence.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: Pull-up Disable.

fields.name: PRLIN
fields.text: 1 stops the LIN/UART clock, shutting it down; reinitialise the LIN after turning it back on.

fields.name: PRSPI
fields.text: 1 stops the SPI clock, shutting it down; reinitialise the SPI after turning it back on. Keep it 0 when the debugWIRE on-chip debugger is used.

fields.name: PRTIM1
fields.text: 1 shuts down Timer/Counter1; on re-enable it carries on as before.

fields.name: PRTIM0
fields.text: 1 shuts down Timer/Counter0 when it is synchronous (AS0 = 0); on re-enable it carries on as before.

fields.name: PRUSI
fields.text: 1 stops the USI clock, shutting it down; reinitialise the USI after turning it back on.

fields.name: PRADC
fields.text: 1 shuts down the ADC, which must be disabled first; while it is off, the ADC input multiplexer is unavailable to the analog comparator.

registers.name: MCUSR
registers.title: MCU Status Register
notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.

fields.name: WDRF
fields.text: Set by a watchdog system reset; a write of 0 or a power-on reset clears it.

fields.name: BORF
fields.text: Set by a brown-out reset; a write of 0 or a power-on reset clears it.

fields.name: EXTRF
fields.text: Set by an external reset; a write of 0 or a power-on reset clears it.

fields.name: PORF
fields.text: Set by a power-on reset; cleared only by writing 0. Reading and then clearing MCUSR early in the program lets the next reset's source be read from these flags.

fields.name: WDIF
fields.text: Set on a watchdog time-out when the watchdog is in interrupt mode; cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. With SREG.I and WDIE set, the watchdog interrupt runs.

fields.name: WDIE
fields.text: 1, with SREG.I set, enables the watchdog interrupt. With WDE 0 the watchdog only interrupts; with WDE 1 it both interrupts and resets: a first time-out sets WDIF, running the vector clears WDIE and WDIF (leaving reset-only operation), and a second time-out before the interrupt runs resets the system. Keeping both needs WDIE set again after each interrupt, outside the interrupt routine. When the watchdog serves as clock monitor, system reset mode is on and interrupt mode is turned off. At least one of WDTON, WDE and WDIE is 1.

fields.name: WDP3
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 3; with WDP[2:0], sets the time-out period while the watchdog runs.

fields.name: WDCE
fields.text: Must be set in the timed sequence that clears WDE or changes the prescaler bits; hardware clears it four clock cycles after it is written 1.

fields.name: WDE
fields.text: Watchdog system reset enable; held at 1 while MCUSR.WDRF is 1, so WDRF must be cleared before WDE can be. This keeps the part resetting while a fault persists and gives a safe start after it.

fields.name: WDP2
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 2; with WDP3, WDP1 and WDP0, sets the time-out period while the watchdog runs.

fields.name: WDP1
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 1; with WDP3, WDP2 and WDP0, sets the time-out period while the watchdog runs.

fields.name: WDP0
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 0; with WDP[3:1], sets the time-out period while the watchdog runs.

fields.name: ISC1
fields.text: Level or edge on pin INT1 that raises External Interrupt 1 (with SREG.I and its mask set). The pin is sampled before edges are found: edge or toggle pulses longer than one clock period always interrupt, shorter ones may not; a low level must last until the current instruction ends.

fields.name: ISC0
fields.text: Level or edge on pin INT0 that raises External Interrupt 0 (with SREG.I and its mask set). The pin is sampled before edges are found: edge or toggle pulses longer than one clock period always interrupt, shorter ones may not; a low level must last until the current instruction ends.

fields.name: INT1
fields.text: 1, with SREG.I set, enables the INT1 pin interrupt, sensed as EICRA.ISC1 sets and served from the INT1 vector; pin activity raises it even when INT1 is an output.

fields.name: INT0
fields.text: 1, with SREG.I set, enables the INT0 pin interrupt, sensed as EICRA.ISC0 sets and served from the INT0 vector; pin activity raises it even when INT0 is an output.

fields.name: INTF1
fields.text: Set when an edge or change on INT1 requests an interrupt; with SREG.I and EIMSK.INT1 set the MCU jumps to the vector. Cleared when the routine runs or by writing 1; always 0 while INT1 is set for level interrupt.

fields.name: INTF0
fields.text: Set when an edge or change on INT0 requests an interrupt; with SREG.I and EIMSK.INT0 set the MCU jumps to the vector. Cleared when the routine runs or by writing 1; always 0 while INT0 is set for level interrupt.

fields.name: PCIE1
fields.text: 1, with SREG.I set, enables pin change interrupt 1: a change on any PCINT[15:8] pin enabled in PCMSK1 runs the PCI1 vector.

fields.name: PCIE0
fields.text: 1, with SREG.I set, enables pin change interrupt 0: a change on any PCINT[7:0] pin enabled in PCMSK0 runs the PCI0 vector.

fields.name: PCIF1
fields.text: Set when a change on a PCINT[15:8] pin requests an interrupt; with SREG.I and PCICR.PCIE1 set the MCU jumps to the vector. Cleared when the routine runs or by writing 1.

fields.name: PCIF0
fields.text: Set when a change on a PCINT[7:0] pin requests an interrupt; with SREG.I and PCICR.PCIE0 set the MCU jumps to the vector. Cleared when the routine runs or by writing 1.

fields.name: PCINT[15:8]
fields.text: One bit per pin PCINT15 to PCINT8: 1 enables that pin's change interrupt (with PCIE1 also set), 0 disables it.

fields.name: PCINT
fields.text: One bit per pin PCINT7 to PCINT0: 1 enables that pin's change interrupt (with PCIE0 also set), 0 disables it.

fields.text: 1 turns off every I/O port pull-up, even on pins whose DDxn and PORTxn are 0 and 1.

fields.name: BBMB

fields.name: BBMA

fields.name: PUDB

fields.name: PUDA

In fast PWM and phase correct PWM, when OCR0A equals TOP with COM0A1 set, the compare match is ignored and the set or clear happens at TOP.

fields.text: Counting sequence, source of TOP and waveform type: normal, CTC, or one of two PWM modes. MAX is 0xFF and BOTTOM is 0x00.

fields.name: FOC0A
fields.text: Writing 1 forces an immediate compare match, so OC0A changes as COM0A sets; it raises no interrupt and does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR0A as TOP. Works only in non-PWM modes; write it 0 when writing TCCR0B in PWM mode. Always reads 0.

fields.name: EXCLK
fields.text: 1, with the asynchronous clock selected, enables the external clock input buffer so a clock on XTAL1 replaces the crystal; set it before choosing asynchronous operation. The crystal oscillator runs only while it is 0.

fields.name: AS0
fields.text: 0 clocks Timer/Counter0 from clkI/O as a synchronous peripheral; 1 clocks it from the low-frequency crystal oscillator or the external clock on XTAL1, as EXCLK selects. Changing it may corrupt TCNT0, OCR0A and TCCR0A. The switch happens only when the system clock comes from the calibrated internal RC oscillator or the watchdog oscillator: AS0 stays 1 if it was allowed, otherwise it is forced to 0.

fields.name: TCN0UB
fields.text: In asynchronous operation, set when TCNT0 is written and cleared by hardware once TCNT0 takes the new value from its temporary register; 0 means TCNT0 can take a new value.

fields.name: OCR0AUB
fields.text: In asynchronous operation, set when OCR0A is written and cleared by hardware once OCR0A takes the new value from its temporary register; 0 means OCR0A can take a new value.

fields.name: TCR0AUB
fields.text: In asynchronous operation, set when TCCR0A is written and cleared by hardware once TCCR0A takes the new value from its temporary register; 0 means TCCR0A can take a new value.

fields.name: TCR0BUB
fields.text: In asynchronous operation, set when TCCR0B is written and cleared by hardware once TCCR0B takes the new value from its temporary register; 0 means TCCR0B can take a new value. Writing any of TCNT0, OCR0A, TCCR0A or TCCR0B while its busy flag is set may corrupt the value and cause a stray interrupt. A read of TCNT0 gives the live count; a read of OCR0A, TCCR0A or TCCR0B gives the temporary register.

fields.name: OCIE0A
fields.text: 1, with SREG.I set, enables the Timer/Counter0 compare match A interrupt, which runs when TIFR0.OCF0A is set.

fields.name: TOIE0
fields.text: 1, with SREG.I set, enables the Timer/Counter0 overflow interrupt, which runs when TIFR0.TOV0 is set.

fields.name: OCF0A
fields.text: Set on a compare match between Timer/Counter0 and OCR0A; cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. With SREG.I, OCIE0A and OCF0A set, the compare match interrupt runs.

fields.name: TOV0
fields.text: Set on a Timer/Counter0 overflow, and in PWM mode when the counter reverses direction at 0x00; cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. With SREG.I, TOIE0 and TOV0 set, the overflow interrupt runs.

fields.name: TSM
fields.text: Timer/Counter Synchronization Mode.

fields.name: PSR0
fields.text: 1 resets the Timer/Counter0 prescaler. Hardware normally clears it at once; in asynchronous mode it stays 1 until the reset is done, and it is not cleared while TSM is set.

fields.name: PSR1
fields.text: Prescaler Reset Timer/Counter1.

fields.name: TSM
fields.text: 1 enters synchronization mode: PSR0 and PSR1 keep the value written, holding their prescalers in reset so the timers stay halted and can be set alike. Writing 0 makes hardware clear PSR0 and PSR1, and the timers start counting together.

fields.name: PSR0
fields.text: Prescaler Reset Timer/Counter0.

fields.name: PSR1
fields.text: 1 resets the Timer/Counter1 prescaler. Hardware normally clears it at once, but not while TSM is set.

fields.name: COM1A
fields.text: OC1Ai pin behaviour; any nonzero setting puts OC1Ai on the pin in place of the port function, though the pin's DDR bit and its TCCR1D.OC1Ai bit must be 1 for the output to drive. The meaning depends on WGM1[3:0]. In fast PWM, when OCR1A equals TOP with COM1A1 set, the compare match is ignored and the set or clear happens at TOP; the phase correct modes also treat OCR1A equal to TOP with COM1A1 set as a special case.

With WGM13 0: OC1A/OC1B off, pin a normal port. With WGM13 1: OC1A toggles on compare match; OC1B reserved.
OC1A/OC1B low on compare match, high at TOP.
OC1A/OC1B high on compare match, low at TOP.

fields.name: COM1B
fields.text: OC1Bi pin behaviour; any nonzero setting puts OC1Bi on the pin in place of the port function, though the pin's DDR bit and its TCCR1D.OC1Bi bit must be 1 for the output to drive. The meaning depends on WGM1[3:0]. In fast PWM, when OCR1B equals TOP with COM1B1 set, the compare match is ignored and the set or clear happens at TOP; the phase correct modes also treat OCR1B equal to TOP with COM1B1 set as a special case.

OC1A/OC1B low on compare match, high at TOP.
OC1A/OC1B high on compare match, low at TOP.

fields.name: WGM1
fields.text: Low two bits of WGM1[3:0], which with WGM1[3:2] in TCCR1B set the counting sequence, source of TOP and waveform type: normal, CTC, or one of three PWM modes. The old names CTC1 and PWM1[1:0] refer to the same bits.

registers.name: TCCR1B
registers.title: Timer/Counter1 Control Register B
notes: The settings of WGM1[3:2] are carried on TCCR1A.WGM1, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: ICNC1
fields.text: 1 filters the ICP1 input: it changes only after four equal samples in a row, delaying the capture by four oscillator cycles.

fields.name: ICES1
fields.text: Capture edge on ICP1: 0 falling, 1 rising. A capture copies the count into ICR1 and sets ICF1, which can raise the input capture interrupt. When ICR1 serves as TOP, ICP1 is disconnected and input capture is off.

fields.name: WGM1[3:2]
fields.text: High two bits of the Timer/Counter1 waveform generation mode, with TCCR1A.WGM1.

fields.name: CS1
fields.text: Clock source for Timer/Counter1. With an external pin source, edges on T1 clock the counter even when T1 is an output, so software can count.

values.text: External clock on T1, falling edge.
External clock on T1, rising edge.

fields.name: FOC1A
fields.text: Writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on channel A, so OC1Ax changes as COM1A and the OC1Ax bits set; it raises no interrupt and does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR1A as TOP. Works only in non-PWM modes; write it 0 whenever TCCR1A is written in a PWM mode. Always reads 0.

fields.name: FOC1B
fields.text: Writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on channel B, so OC1Bx changes as COM1B and the OC1Bx bits set; it raises no interrupt and does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR1A as TOP. Works only in non-PWM modes; write it 0 whenever TCCR1A is written in a PWM mode. Always reads 0.

fields.name: OC1BX
fields.text: Enables channel B output compare pin OC1BX.

fields.name: OC1BW
fields.text: Enables channel B output compare pin OC1BW.

fields.name: OC1BV
fields.text: Enables channel B output compare pin OC1BV.

fields.name: OC1BU
fields.text: Enables channel B output compare pin OC1BU.

fields.name: OC1AX
fields.text: Enables channel A output compare pin OC1AX.

fields.name: OC1AW
fields.text: Enables channel A output compare pin OC1AW.

fields.name: OC1AV
fields.text: Enables channel A output compare pin OC1AV.

fields.name: OC1AU
fields.text: Enables channel A output compare pin OC1AU.

fields.name: TCNT1[15:8]
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 count, high byte.

fields.name: TCNT1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 count, low byte.

fields.name: OCR1A[15:8]
fields.text: Output Compare Register 1A, high byte.

fields.name: OCR1A
fields.text: Output Compare Register 1A, low byte.

fields.name: OCR1B[15:8]
fields.text: Output Compare Register 1B, high byte.

fields.name: OCR1B
fields.text: Output Compare Register 1B, low byte.

fields.name: ICR1[15:8]
fields.text: Input Capture Register 1, high byte.

fields.name: ICR1
fields.text: Input Capture Register 1, low byte.

fields.name: ICIE1
fields.text: 1, with SREG.I set, enables the Timer/Counter1 input capture interrupt, which runs when TIFR1.ICF1 is set.

fields.name: OCIE1B
fields.text: 1, with SREG.I set, enables the Timer/Counter1 compare match B interrupt, which runs when TIFR1.OCF1B is set.

fields.name: OCIE1A
fields.text: 1, with SREG.I set, enables the Timer/Counter1 compare match A interrupt, which runs when TIFR1.OCF1A is set.

fields.name: TOIE1
fields.text: 1, with SREG.I set, enables the Timer/Counter1 overflow interrupt, which runs when TIFR1.TOV1 is set.

fields.name: ICF1
fields.text: Set by a capture event on ICP1, or, when WGM1 makes ICR1 the TOP, when the counter reaches TOP. Cleared when the input capture vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: OCF1B
fields.text: Set in the timer clock cycle after TCNT1 matches OCR1B; a FOC1B strobe does not set it. Cleared when the compare match B vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: OCF1A
fields.text: Set in the timer clock cycle after TCNT1 matches OCR1A; a FOC1A strobe does not set it. Cleared when the compare match A vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: TOV1
fields.text: Overflow flag whose setting depends on WGM1[3:0]; in normal and CTC modes it is set when the timer overflows. Cleared when the overflow vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: SPIE
fields.text: Set to have the SPI interrupt run when SPSR.SPIF is set and the global interrupt bit in SREG is set.

fields.name: SPE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the SPI on; no SPI operation works while it is 0.

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: 1 shifts the data word out LSB first; 0 shifts it out MSB first.

fields.name: MSTR
fields.text: 1 selects SPI master, 0 selects slave. With SS an input pulled low while MSTR is 1, hardware clears MSTR and sets SPSR.SPIF; MSTR must then be written 1 again to return to master.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: Idle level of SCK: 1 = high when idle, 0 = low when idle.

fields.name: CPHA
fields.text: 0 samples data on the first (leading) SCK edge; 1 samples it on the last (trailing) one.

fields.name: SPR
fields.text: With SPSR.SPI2X, sets the SCK rate as a division of fclkio when the device is master; no effect in slave.

registers.name: SPSR
registers.title: SPI Status Register
notes: The settings of SPI2X are carried on SPCR.SPR, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: SPIF
fields.text: Set when a serial transfer finishes, and in master mode when SS is an input driven low. Raises an interrupt if SPCR.SPIE and global interrupts are on. Cleared by hardware on entering the interrupt vector, or by reading SPSR with SPIF set and then accessing SPDR.

fields.name: WCOL
fields.text: Set when SPDR is written while a transfer is in progress. Cleared, together with SPIF, by reading SPSR with WCOL set and then accessing SPDR.

fields.name: SPI2X
fields.text: 1 doubles the SCK frequency in master mode, giving a shortest SCK period of two CPU clocks. As slave the SPI is guaranteed only at fclkio/4 or slower. The SPI is also the port for serial downloading and uploading of program memory and EEPROM.

fields.name: SPD
fields.text: Read/write port that moves data to and from the SPI shift register: writing it starts sending, reading it returns the receive buffer.

fields.name: USID
fields.text: Direct access to the USI serial (shift) register. A write in the same cycle as a serial clock keeps the written value with no shift. It shifts left on the clock picked by USICS[1:0]: an external edge, a Timer/Counter0 compare match, or the USICLK strobe; DI/SDA and USCK/SCL still reach it with USIWM[1:0] = 00. Bit 7 drives the output pin (DO or SDA) through a latch that is transparent during the first half of the clock with an external source (USICS1 = 1) and always with an internal one (USICS1 = 0); a new MSB appears at once while the latch is open, and input sampling and output change fall on opposite edges. The pin's DDR bit must be 1 for the output to reach the pin.

fields.name: USIB
fields.text: Receives a copy of the serial register when a transfer completes, so the CPU can read received data from here instead of USIDR with less timing pressure. Reading it sets the USI flags as reading USIDR does.

fields.name: USISIF
fields.text: In Two-wire mode, set on a start condition; in output-disable or Three-wire mode with USICS = 11 and USICLK = 0, or USICS = 10 and USICLK = 0, set by any edge on SCK. Raises an interrupt when USICR.USISIE and the global interrupt flag are set. Cleared only by writing 1, which also releases the start-detect hold of USCL in Two-wire mode. This interrupt wakes the device from every sleep mode.

fields.name: USIOIF
fields.text: Set when the 4-bit counter wraps from 15 to 0. Raises an interrupt when USICR.USIOIE and the global interrupt flag are set. Cleared only by writing 1; doing so lets go of SCL where Two-wire mode held it on overflow. This interrupt wakes the device from Idle sleep.

fields.name: USIPF
fields.text: In Two-wire mode, set on a stop condition; cleared by writing 1. It raises no interrupt; it serves Two-wire bus master arbitration.

fields.name: USIDC
fields.text: Reads 1 when USIDR bit 7 does not match the level on the pin. Valid only in Two-wire mode; it serves Two-wire bus master arbitration.

fields.name: USICNT
fields.text: The 4-bit counter, readable and writable by the CPU. It counts once per clock from the external edge detector, a Timer/Counter0 compare match, or the USICLK or USITC strobes, as chosen by USICS[1:0]. With an external source (USICS1 = 1), writing 1 to USICLK lets a write to USITC clock it. USCK/SCL still clocks it with USIWM[1:0] = 00.

fields.name: USISIE
fields.text: 1 enables the start-condition interrupt. A pending one runs at once when USISIE and the global interrupt flag are both 1.

fields.name: USIOIE
fields.text: 1 enables the counter-overflow interrupt. A pending one runs at once when USIOIE and the global interrupt flag are both 1.

fields.name: USIWM
fields.text: Wire mode. It changes only how the outputs behave; data and clock inputs work the same in every mode, so the counter and USIDR can be clocked externally and data sampled with outputs off. In Two-wire mode DI and USCK are called SDA and SCL.

values.text: Outputs, clock hold and start detector off; pins work as normal port pins.

Three-wire mode on DO, DI and USCK. DO overrides its PORT bit but the DDR bit still sets direction, and as an input its pull-up follows PORT. DI and USCK leave normal port operation alone. A master makes clock pulses in software by toggling PORT with the pin set as output, for which USICR.USITC can be used.

Two-wire mode on SDA (DI) and SCL (USCK), both bidirectional open-collector, drivers enabled by their DDR bits. An enabled SDA driver pulls SDA low when the USIDR output or its PORT bit is 0, else releases it. An enabled SCL driver pulls SCL low when its PORT bit is 0 or the start detector holds it, else releases it; a detected start holds SCL low until USISIF is cleared. Inputs are unaffected; pull-ups on SDA and SCL are off.
Two-wire mode on SDA and SCL as for 10, but SCL is also held low on a counter overflow until USIOIF is cleared.

fields.name: USICS
fields.text: Clock source for USIDR and the counter. With the external clock (USCK/SCL) the output latch changes the output on the edge opposite to input sampling; with the software strobe or Timer/Counter0 compare match the latch is transparent and the output changes at once. 00 selects the software strobe, where writing 1 to USICLK clocks USIDR and the counter. With USICS1 = 1, USICLK stops being a strobe and instead chooses between external clocking and software clocking by USITC.

fields.name: USICLK
fields.text: With USICS[1:0] = 00, writing 1 shifts USIDR one step and increments the counter; the output changes in the same instruction cycle and the bit shifted in was sampled in the cycle before. With an external clock (USICS1 = 1) it acts as a select bit instead: 1 makes the USITC strobe the counter's clock. Reads 0.

fields.name: USITC
fields.text: Writing 1 toggles USCK/SCL between 0 and 1, whatever the DDR setting; DDB2 must be 1 for the value to show on the pin. With USICS1 = 1 and USICLK = 1, a write here also clocks the 4-bit counter directly, so a master can see the end of a transfer early. Reads 0.

fields.name: USIPOS
fields.text: Writing it moves the USI to its other set of pins.

peripherals.name: LIN
peripherals.title: LIN / UART - Local Interconnect Network Controller or UART

fields.name: LSWRES
fields.text: 0 = no action; 1 = software reset of the LIN/UART, the bit clearing itself when the reset ends.

values.text: Software reset; the bit clears itself when the reset is done.

fields.name: LIN13
fields.text: 0 = LIN 2.1 (default); 1 = LIN 1.3.

fields.name: LCONF
fields.text: Configuration, default 00. LIN mode: 00 = standard (CRC on, Frame_Time_Out on, listen off); 01 = no CRC and no Frame_Time_Out (listen off); 10 = no Frame_Time_Out (CRC on, listen off); 11 = listening (CRC on, Frame_Time_Out on). UART mode: 00 = 8-bit, no parity; 01 = 8-bit, even parity; 10 = 8-bit, odd parity (all with listen off); 11 = listening, 8-bit, no parity.

values.text: Standard: CRC on, Frame_Time_Out on, listening off.
CRC off, Frame_Time_Out off, listening off.
Frame_Time_Out off; CRC on, listening off.
Listens only, with both CRC and Frame_Time_Out on.

fields.name: LENA
fields.text: 0 = LIN/UART disabled; 1 = enabled. Applies to both LIN and UART modes.

values.text: Off, in LIN and UART modes.
On, in LIN and UART modes.

fields.name: LCMD
fields.text: Command and mode; acts only while LENA is 1. 000 = receive header, or abort (LIN); 001 = send header (LIN); 010 = receive response (LIN); 011 = send response (LIN); 100 = UART byte receive and send both off; 11x = UART byte receive on; 1x1 = UART byte send on.

values.text: UART: byte receive and transmit off.

fields.name: LIDST
fields.text: Identifier status: 0xx = no particular identifier; 100 = identifier 60 (0x3C); 101 = 61 (0x3D); 110 = 62 (0x3E); 111 = 63 (0x3F).

fields.name: LBUSY
fields.text: 0 = idle; 1 = busy receiving or transmitting.

fields.name: LERR
fields.text: OR of the LINERR bits: 0 = no error, 1 = an error occurred. Raises an interrupt when LINENIR.LENERR is set. Writing 1 clears it and every LINERR bit; in UART mode a read of LINDAT also clears it.

fields.name: LIDOK
fields.text: 0 = no identifier; 1 = as slave, an identifier is present, as master, the Tx header is done. Raises an interrupt when LINENIR.LENIDOK is set; writing 1 clears it.

values.text: Slave: identifier present. Master: Tx header done.

fields.name: LTXOK
fields.text: 0 = nothing sent; 1 = Tx response done. Raises an interrupt when LINENIR.LENTXOK is set; writing 1 clears it, and in UART mode so does a write of LINDAT.

fields.name: LRXOK
fields.text: 0 = nothing received; 1 = Rx response done. Raises an interrupt when LINENIR.LENRXOK is set; writing 1 clears it, and in UART mode so does a read of LINDAT.

fields.name: LENERR
fields.text: 0 = error interrupt masked; 1 = enabled.

fields.name: LENIDOK
fields.text: 0 = identifier interrupt masked; 1 = enabled.

fields.name: LENTXOK
fields.text: 0 = transmit-done interrupt masked; 1 = enabled.

fields.name: LENRXOK
fields.text: 0 = receive-done interrupt masked; 1 = enabled.

fields.name: LABORT
fields.text: 0 = no warning; 1 = a LIN abort command took place. Cleared along with LINSIR.LERR.

values.name: LIN abort command occurred
values.text: A LIN abort command took place.

fields.name: LTOERR
fields.text: 0 = no error; 1 = Frame_Time_Out error. Cleared along with LINSIR.LERR.

fields.name: LOVERR
fields.text: 0 = no error; 1 = overrun error. Cleared along with LINSIR.LERR.

fields.name: LFERR
fields.text: 0 = no error; 1 = framing error. Cleared along with LINSIR.LERR.

fields.name: LSERR
fields.text: 0 = no error; 1 = synchronization error. Cleared along with LINSIR.LERR.

fields.name: LPERR
fields.text: 0 = no error; 1 = parity error. Cleared along with LINSIR.LERR.

fields.name: LCERR
fields.text: 0 = no error; 1 = checksum error. Cleared along with LINSIR.LERR.

fields.name: LBERR
fields.text: 0 = no error; 1 = bit error. Cleared along with LINSIR.LERR.

fields.name: LDISR
fields.text: 0 = bit-timing resynchronization on (default); 1 = off.

fields.name: LBT
fields.text: Samples taken per bit, each sample lasting (LDIV[11:0] + 1) / fclkI/O. Default 32, minimum 8, maximum 63.

fields.name: LDIV
fields.text: Low eight bits of LDIV, the divider applied to clkI/O to set the LIN or UART baud rate.

fields.name: LDIV[11:8]
fields.text: High four bits of LDIV, the divider applied to clkI/O to set the LIN or UART baud rate.

fields.name: LTXDL
fields.text: LIN mode: number of bytes to send, capped at 8. Unused in UART mode.

fields.name: LRXDL
fields.text: LIN mode: number of bytes to receive, capped at 8. Unused in UART mode.

fields.name: LP
fields.text: LIN mode: identifier parity, LP0 = LID4 xor LID2 xor LID1 xor LID0 and LP1 = not (LID1 xor LID3 xor LID4 xor LID5). Unused in UART mode.

fields.name: LID5/LDL1
fields.text: LIN 2.1: identifier bit 5 (six-bit identifier, no length carried). LIN 1.3: LDL1, high bit of the data length code LDL[1:0]: 00 or 01 = 2-byte response, 10 = 4 bytes, 11 = 8 bytes. Unused in UART mode.

fields.name: LID4/LDL0
fields.text: LIN 2.1: identifier bit 4 (six-bit identifier, no length carried). LIN 1.3: LDL0, low bit of the data length code LDL[1:0]: 00 or 01 = 2-byte response, 10 = 4 bytes, 11 = 8 bytes. Unused in UART mode.

fields.name: LID
fields.text: Identifier bits 3:0: the whole four-bit identifier in LIN 1.3, the low four bits of the six-bit identifier in LIN 2.1. Unused in UART mode.

registers.name: LINSEL
registers.title: LIN Data Buffer Selection Register
notes: Initial value of bits 7:4 printed as –.

fields.name: LAINC
fields.text: LIN mode: 0 = the FIFO data buffer index steps on by itself (default); 1 = it does not. Unused in UART mode.

values.text: FIFO data buffer index steps on by itself (default).

fields.name: LINDX
fields.text: LIN mode: position of the response data byte in the FIFO data buffer, which is reached through LINDAT. Unused in UART mode.

fields.name: LDATA
fields.text: LIN mode: port to the FIFO data buffer. UART mode: the data register, with no buffer or FIFO. A write sends data out; a read returns received data.

fields.name: AREFEN
fields.text: External Voltage Reference Input Enable.

fields.name: XREFEN
fields.text: Internal Voltage Reference Output Enable.

fields.name: ISRCEN
fields.text: Write 1 to switch the current source on. Using the matching DIDR bit while it is on, and switching the source off as soon as possible (for instance once the ADC reading is done), is recommended.

fields.name: REFS
fields.text: With AMISCR.AREFEN, picks the ADC voltage reference. A change during a conversion takes effect only when it ends (ADCSRA.ADIF set), and the conversion after any change takes 25 ADC clocks. With active channels, AVCC or an external AREF above AVCC - 1 V degrades ADC accuracy. The internal references cannot be used while an external voltage is applied on AREF.

rows: AVCC is the reference, disconnected from the AREF pin.
External reference on the AREF pin (AREF at least 2.0 V).

fields.name: ADLAR
fields.text: 1 left-adjusts the conversion result in ADCH:ADCL; 0 right-adjusts it. A change takes effect in the data register at once, even mid-conversion.

fields.name: MUX
fields.text: Picks the analog inputs connected to the ADC and, for differential inputs, the gain. A change during a conversion takes effect only when it ends (ADCSRA.ADIF set).

registers.name: ADCSRA
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register A

fields.name: ADEN
fields.text: 1 turns the ADC on, 0 turns it off; turning it off ends any conversion in progress.

fields.name: ADSC
fields.text: Write 1 to start a conversion in single-conversion mode, or the first conversion in free-running mode. The first conversion after the ADC is enabled, or started together with enabling, initializes the ADC and takes 25 ADC clocks instead of 13. Reads 1 while a conversion runs and 0 once it is done; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ADATE
fields.text: 1 enables auto triggering: a conversion starts on a rising edge of the trigger signal picked by ADCSRB.ADTS.

fields.name: ADIF
fields.text: Set when a conversion finishes and the data registers hold the result. The conversion-complete interrupt runs if ADIE and the SREG I-bit are set. Cleared by hardware on entering the vector, or by writing 1. A read-modify-write of ADCSRA, SBI and CBI included, can disable a pending interrupt.

fields.name: ADIE
fields.text: With the SREG I-bit set, 1 enables the ADC conversion-complete interrupt.

fields.name: ADPS
fields.text: Division factor from the system clock to the ADC clock.

fields.name: ADC9
fields.text: ADC result bit 9 (ADLAR = 0).

fields.name: ADC8
fields.text: ADC result bit 8 (ADLAR = 0).

fields.text: ADC result bit 9 (ADLAR = 1).

fields.text: ADC result bit 8 (ADLAR = 1).

registers.name: ADCSRB
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register B

fields.name: BIN
fields.text: Gain stage mode: 0 = unipolar (default), 1 = bipolar. Unipolar converts one-sided only, needs the positive input above the negative one or the result saturates at the reference, and gives 10 bits. Bipolar converts two-sided and gives 9 bits plus sign in two's complement.

fields.name: ACME
fields.text: Analog Comparator Multiplexer Enable.

fields.name: ACIR1
fields.text: Analog Comparator Internal Voltage Reference Select, bit 1.

fields.name: ACIR0
fields.text: Analog Comparator Internal Voltage Reference Select, bit 0.

fields.name: ADTS
fields.text: With ADCSRA.ADATE = 1, picks the source whose interrupt flag's rising edge starts a conversion; with ADATE = 0 it has no effect. Moving from a cleared source to a set one makes a rising edge, which starts a conversion if ADCSRA.ADEN is set. Moving to free-running (000) does not trigger, even with ADIF set.

fields.name: ADC7D/AIN1D
fields.text: 1 disables the digital input buffer on the ADC7 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Setting it when the pin carries only an analog signal saves the buffer's power.

fields.name: ADC6D/AIN0D
fields.text: 1 disables the digital input buffer on the ADC6 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Setting it when the pin carries only an analog signal saves the buffer's power.

fields.name: ADC5D
fields.text: 1 disables the digital input buffer on the ADC5 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Setting it when the pin carries only an analog signal saves the buffer's power.

fields.name: ADC1D

fields.name: ADC0D
fields.text: 1 disables the digital input buffer on the ADC0 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Setting it when the pin carries only an analog signal saves the buffer's power.

fields.name: ADC10D
fields.text: 1 disables the digital input buffer on the ADC10 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Setting it when the pin carries only an analog signal saves the buffer's power.

registers.name: AMISCR
registers.title: Analog Miscellaneous Control Register
notes: The settings of AREFEN are carried on ADMUX.REFS, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: AREFEN
fields.text: 1 takes the ADC voltage reference from the AREF pin. With active channels, AVCC or an external AREF above AVCC - 1 V degrades ADC accuracy, and the internal references cannot be used while an external voltage is on AREF. Setting the pin's DIDR bit while AREFEN is 1 is recommended.

fields.name: XREFEN
fields.text: 1 puts the internal 1.1 V or 2.56 V reference out on the XREF pin. Setting the pin's DIDR bit while XREFEN is 1 is recommended.

fields.name: ISRCEN
fields.text: Current Source Enable.

registers.name: ADCSRB
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register B

fields.name: BIN
fields.text: Bipolar Input Mode.

fields.name: ACME
fields.text: With the ADC off (ADCSRA.ADEN = 0), 1 lets the ADC multiplexer pick the comparator's positive input; 0 puts AIN1 there. With the ADC set for single-ended inputs, MUX[4:0] can then route any ADC[10:0] pin to it, which needs the ADC switched off.

fields.name: ACIR
fields.text: When ACIRS is set, picks the internal voltage reference fed to the comparator's negative input.

registers.title: Analog Comparator Control and Status Register
notes: Initial value of bit 5 printed as N/A.
The settings of ACIRS are carried on ADCSRB.ACIR, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: ACD
fields.text: 1 cuts power to the analog comparator, at any time, lowering consumption in Active and Idle. Clear ACIE before changing ACD, or the change can raise an interrupt.

fields.name: ACIRS
fields.text: 1 puts an internal reference voltage on the comparator's negative input; 0 puts AIN0 there.

fields.name: ACO
fields.text: The comparator output after synchronization, which delays it by 1 to 2 clocks.

fields.name: ACI
fields.text: Hardware sets it when the comparator output does what ACIS1:0 selects. The comparator interrupt runs if ACIE and the SREG I-bit are set. Cleared by hardware on entering the vector, or by writing 1.

fields.name: ACIE
fields.text: With the SREG I-bit set, 1 enables the comparator interrupt; 0 disables it.

fields.name: ACIC
fields.text: 1 connects the comparator output straight to the Timer/Counter1 input capture front end, so it uses that unit's noise canceler and edge select; 0 leaves them unconnected. TIMSK1.ICIE1 must be set for the comparator to raise the input capture interrupt.

fields.name: ACIS
fields.text: Which comparator events raise the interrupt. Clear ACIE before changing these bits, or the change can raise an interrupt.

fields.name: ADC7D/AIN1D
fields.text: 1 disables the digital input buffer on the AIN1 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Setting it when the pin carries only an analog signal saves the buffer's power.

fields.name: ADC6D/AIN0D
fields.text: 1 disables the digital input buffer on the AIN0 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Setting it when the pin carries only an analog signal saves the buffer's power.

registers.name: SPMCSR
registers.title: Store Program Memory Control and Status Register

fields.name: RWWSB
fields.text: Kept for compatibility with Read-While-Write parts; always reads 0 on ATtiny87/167.

fields.name: SIGRD
fields.text: Written 1 together with SPMEN, makes an LPM within the next three clocks read a signature-row byte into the destination register. An SPM within four clocks after SIGRD and SPMEN are set does nothing.

fields.name: CTPB
fields.text: A write of this bit while the temporary page buffer is being filled clears the buffer, losing its data.

fields.name: RFLB
fields.text: After RFLB and SPMEN are set, an LPM within three clocks reads the lock bits or the fuse bits, chosen by Z0 of the Z-pointer, into the destination register.

fields.name: PGWRT
fields.text: Written 1 together with SPMEN, makes an SPM within the next four clocks write the temporary buffer to the page addressed by the high part of Z; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the write ends or if no SPM comes within four clocks. The CPU halts for the whole page write.

fields.name: PGERS
fields.text: Written 1 together with SPMEN, makes an SPM within the next four clocks erase the page addressed by the high part of Z; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the erase ends or if no SPM comes within four clocks. The CPU halts for the whole operation.

fields.name: SPMEN
fields.text: Enables SPM for the next four clocks. Written with SIGRD, CTPB, RFLB, PGWRT or PGERS, the next SPM does that operation; written alone, the next SPM stores R1:R0 in the temporary page buffer at the Z address, ignoring Z's LSB. Clears itself when the SPM ends or if none comes within four clocks; stays 1 through a page erase or write until it finishes. Lower-six-bit values other than 100001, 010001, 001001, 000101, 000011 and 000001 do nothing. Only one SPM should be active at a time.
